reference.source: Volpe's Neurology of the Newborn / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: A lethal autosomal recessive ciliopathy classically defined by the triad of occipital encephalocele, bilateral enlarged cystic (polycystic) kidneys, and postaxial polydactyly
Hepatic involvement with ductal plate malformation and fibrosis is a further consistent feature, and many consider the hepatic changes near-universal
It sits at the severe end of the ciliopathy spectrum and shares causative genes with Joubert syndrome and other ciliopathies, illustrating phenotype overlap
The massively enlarged kidneys cause oligohydramnios, leading to pulmonary hypoplasia and the Potter sequence of features
Prenatal diagnosis is often possible in the first or early second trimester from the combination of encephalocele, large echogenic cystic kidneys, and polydactyly on ultrasound
Additional malformations may include other posterior fossa or neural tube defects, cleft lip or palate, and genital anomalies
Diagnosis is clinical and radiological, supported by molecular testing, and is important for recurrence-risk counselling given the twenty-five percent recurrence in future pregnancies
reference.pathophysiology: Meckel-Gruber syndrome is a severe ciliopathy caused by biallelic variants in genes encoding proteins of the ciliary transition zone and basal body. Loss of normal primary cilium function disrupts developmental signalling across multiple organs during embryogenesis, producing central nervous system malformation (typically an occipital encephalocele), cystic dysplasia of the renal collecting system, ductal plate malformation of the liver, and limb patterning defects manifesting as polydactyly. The renal enlargement reduces amniotic fluid, and the consequent oligohydramnios impairs lung development.
additionalDifferentials: Joubert syndrome and related disorders at the milder end of the ciliopathy spectrum
Trisomy 13 with overlapping midline and polydactyly features
Autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease with encephalocele
Isolated neural tube defect with incidental renal anomaly
additionalInvestigations: Detailed foetal ultrasound and, where available, foetal MRI to define the encephalocele and renal cystic disease
Postnatal or post-mortem examination and imaging to document the classic triad
Molecular genetic testing using a ciliopathy panel or exome sequencing
Renal ultrasound to characterise cystic dysplasia and measure kidney size
Liver imaging and histology for ductal plate malformation and fibrosis
Karyotype or microarray to exclude chromosomal differentials such as trisomy 13
redFlags: Severe oligohydramnios with pulmonary hypoplasia incompatible with sustained postnatal breathing
Large occipital encephalocele with neural tissue herniation
Rapidly enlarging cystic kidneys causing abdominal distension and renal failure
Multi-organ malformation indicating a lethal prognosis requiring sensitive counselling
reference.prognosis: Meckel-Gruber syndrome is uniformly lethal, with death occurring before birth or within the neonatal period, chiefly from pulmonary hypoplasia and renal failure. Management is directed at prenatal diagnosis, compassionate perinatal care, and genetic counselling for recurrence risk.
pitfalls: Confusing milder ciliopathies such as Joubert syndrome with the lethal Meckel-Gruber phenotype because of shared genes
Overlooking hepatic ductal plate malformation, which may be less clinically obvious than the renal and CNS features
Failing to offer post-mortem examination and genetic testing, losing the opportunity for accurate recurrence counselling
Attributing the pulmonary hypoplasia to a primary lung problem rather than to oligohydramnios from renal disease
